title: Seizure Medications
desc: Maintenance antiseizure drugs (phenobarbital, levetiracetam IR/XR, zonisamide, KBr), emergency protocols, refractory status, cluster prevention. Includes XR tablet-splitting evidence.

keppra_xr.caption: Levetiracetam XR dissolution study: split XR tablets provide a smooth, sustained-release profile nearly identical to intact XR — making tablet-splitting clinically appropriate for small patients who need a fractional dose. Crushed XR behaves like immediate-release (rapid absorption, plateau). Intact IR and crushed XR are both suitable options when a rapid effect is needed.
keppra_xr.alt: Graph showing levetiracetam drug release (%) over 8 hours for intact XR, split XR, crushed XR, and intact IR — split XR closely follows intact XR

notes.xr_split: Extended-release levetiracetam tablets CAN be split for small dogs. Dissolution studies confirm split XR tablets maintain a sustained-release profile nearly identical to intact XR. Crushed XR behaves like immediate-release.
notes.clustering: Cluster rescue: Keppra 60 mg/kg PO once (regular formulation — NOT XR), then resume maintenance dosing (20 mg/kg TID or 30 mg/kg XR BID).
notes.pre_ictal: Pre-ictal / cluster prevention: Clorazepate 0.5–1 mg/kg q 8 h. Consider giving for 2 days post-seizure to prevent clustering. Higher doses may be used as dictated by side effects.
notes.side_effects: Side effects (sedation, ataxia) are common when starting antiseizure medications and typically improve significantly with time.
notes.status_sequence: Active seizure sequence: (1) Diazepam IV → (2) If 2+ seizures after diazepam, add phenobarbital IV → (3) Levetiracetam IV may be given concurrently. Crushed ER Keppra shows similar kinetics to IR — levels within 30 min.

meds.name: Phenobarbital
meds.desc: first-line antiseizure — monitor serum levels
meds.note: Target serum level 20–40 µg/ml. Recheck level, CBC, and chemistry at 2 weeks then every 6 months.

meds.name: Levetiracetam (regular)
meds.desc: first-line — preferred by many neurologists; no hepatotoxicity, minimal drug interactions

meds.name: Levetiracetam XR
meds.desc: extended-release — BID dosing improves compliance; tablets may be split for small dogs
meds.note: SPLITTING IS APPROPRIATE — dissolution studies confirm split XR maintains sustained-release kinetics. See graph below.

meds.name: Zonisamide
freqs: once daily (SID) if not on PB — 5 mg/kg
meds.desc: first-line or add-on antiseizure
meds.note: If NOT on phenobarbital: 5 mg/kg BID or SID. If ON phenobarbital (induces metabolism): 10 mg/kg BID.

meds.name: Potassium Bromide
meds.desc: add-on antiseizure; slow to steady state (months without loading)
meds.note: Takes 3–4 months to reach steady state without a loading dose. NOT recommended in cats (causes respiratory disease).

meds.name: Gabapentin
meds.desc: add-on antiseizure; also useful for pain and anxiety

meds.name: Pregabalin
meds.desc: add-on antiseizure; similar mechanism to gabapentin

meds.name: Topiramate
meds.desc: add-on antiseizure
meds.note: Alternative dosing: 2.5–5 mg/kg TID. Side effects (sedation, ataxia) typically improve with time.

meds.name: Felbamate
meds.desc: add-on for refractory cases — monitor for aplastic anemia and hepatotoxicity

meds.name: Clorazepate
meds.desc: benzodiazepine for pre-ictal use or post-seizure cluster prevention

meds.name: Levetiracetam — cluster loading
freqs: once only, then resume maintenance dosing
meds.desc: cluster rescue dose — give regular (IR) Keppra once PO, then restart 20 mg/kg TID or 30 mg/kg XR BID
meds.note: Use REGULAR (immediate-release) Keppra only for this loading dose — NOT extended release.

meds.name: Diazepam IV
meds.desc: first-line for active seizure — repeat once if seizure continues

meds.name: Intranasal Midazolam
meds.desc: use if IV access not immediately available

meds.name: Rectal / Intranasal Diazepam
meds.desc: home rescue medication or pre-hospital use

meds.name: Levetiracetam IV
meds.desc: slow bolus over 5–15 min; dilute 1:1 or 1:10 with saline or D5W
meds.note: May be given concurrently with diazepam. Crushed ER Keppra achieves therapeutic levels within 30 min if IV formulation unavailable.

meds.name: Phenobarbital IV
meds.desc: give if 2+ seizures occur despite diazepam
meds.note: 2–8 mg/kg IV. May give IM in cats.

meds.name: Ketamine
meds.bodyFn: (kg,lb)=>'1 mg/kg IV loading dose'+(kg===null?'':' → '+fmtMg(kg)+' mg ('+R2(kg/100)+' ml of 100 mg/ml)')+', then 1 mg/kg/hr CRI. Follow with Dexdomitor.'
meds.lineFn: (kg,lb)=>'1 mg/kg IV'+(kg===null?'':' ('+fmtMg(kg)+' mg, '+R2(kg/100)+' ml of 100 mg/ml)')+', then 1 mg/kg/hr CRI.'
meds.desc: refractory status epilepticus — use with Dexdomitor CRI

meds.name: Dexdomitor
meds.bodyFn: (kg,lb)=>'3 mcg/kg IV loading dose'+(kg===null?'':' → '+fmtMg(3*kg)+' mcg ('+R2(3*kg/500)+' ml of 500 mcg/ml)')+', then 3–7 mcg/kg/hr CRI.'
meds.lineFn: (kg,lb)=>'3 mcg/kg IV'+(kg===null?'':' ('+fmtMg(3*kg)+' mcg, '+R2(3*kg/500)+' ml of 500 mcg/ml)')+', then 3–7 mcg/kg/hr CRI.'
meds.desc: refractory status epilepticus CRI — follow Ketamine loading

meds.name: Phenobarbital
meds.desc: first-line in cats — not hepatotoxic but expect ~30% rise in ALP & ALT
meds.note: Not hepatotoxic in cats, but may see ~30% increases in ALP and ALT. Target serum level 20–40 µg/ml.

meds.name: Levetiracetam
meds.desc: first-line in cats; preferred by many neurologists

meds.name: Zonisamide
meds.desc: second-line or add-on in cats

meds.name: Levetiracetam (third-line add-on)
meds.desc: add-on after phenobarb and zonisamide

meds.name: Clonazepam
meds.desc: benzodiazepine add-on for cats

meds.name: Topiramate
meds.desc: add-on antiseizure for cats

meds.name: Felbamate
meds.desc: add-on for refractory cases

meds.name: Clorazepate
meds.desc: benzodiazepine add-on for cats

meds.name: Diazepam IV
meds.desc: first-line for active seizure in cats

meds.name: Levetiracetam IV
meds.desc: slow bolus over 5–15 min; dilute 1:1 or 1:10 with saline or D5W

meds.name: Phenobarbital IV/IM
meds.desc: if 2+ seizures after diazepam; can give IM in cats
